business_scope.primary_industry_name: Fleet Route Optimization and Real-Time Telematics SaaS

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — unitary national legal system with a common-law, Delaware-influenced statutory corporate law, constitutional and customary-law recognition of traditional land and societal norms, and an autonomous national company registry.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association between the United States of America and the Republic of the Marshall Islands, as amended (economic relations and investment facilitation)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus), in force 13 December 2020
RMI-United States economic assistance and consular facilitation arrangements under the Compact framework (not an OECD-model bilateral investment treaty)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Business Corporations Act 1990, as amended, together with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2012, as amended, the Financial Intelligence Unit Regulations, and the RMI Registrar of Corporations Beneficial Ownership Reporting Rules, requiring licensed registered agents to collect, verify and maintain UBO records for inspection by the RMI Registrar and Financial Intelligence Unit.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the RMI Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, or consular legalization in non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws / Memorandum and Articles of Association
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporator and registered agent on file with the RMI Registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, as required by the destination bank or authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Status
Notarized registered agent acceptance and UBO declaration form
Initial directors' and shareholders' resolutions for incorporation and banking onboarding
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company secretary, directors and notary public

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory adverse-media and watchlist screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, beneficial owners and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council sanctions, EU consolidated sanctions lists, UK sanctions and RMI FIU domestic designations. Full identification of politically exposed persons, including family members and close associates, followed by enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification and senior-management approval. The licensed registered agent must retain immutable screening records for at least five years and report suspicious transactions to the RMI FIU under the AML/CFT Act 2012.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RMI Corporate Registry — Office of the Registrar of Corporations (online name clearance and filing are effectuated through licensed RMI registered agents; no direct public self-service portal is available)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin-script English letters and Arabic numerals. The RMI Registrar does not register corporate names in foreign scripts. Any proposed foreign-language name must be accompanied by an official English transliteration or translation, and the statutory name on the Certificate of Incorporation must remain in Latin script.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended for one further 30-day period if the licensed registered agent requests the extension before expiry. If the Registrar rejects the proposed name, the applicant or registered agent may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar within 14 calendar days, attaching the rejection notice, evidence of distinctiveness, written consents or regulatory approvals for sensitive tokens, and any requested alternative name. The Registrar must respond within 15 business days. Further judicial review lies to the RMI High Court under the Business Corporations Act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not a permissible substitute for the statutory registered office. The Business Corporations Act requires a physical street address in the Republic of the Marshall Islands, maintained continuously by a licensed RMI registered agent. Virtual office services may be used only as a non-statutory business correspondence address for the logistics-technology operations, while legal records, the registered agent file and the UBO register remain at the agent's physical RMI office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to medium for a standard non-resident low-risk SaaS entity. Estimated annual probability of Registrar or FIU inspection of the registered agent's records and UBO files is 5 to 10 percent. Unannounced physical inspection of the company's actual operational premises is unlikely unless the company establishes local employees, physical assets or a predicate AML trigger.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act (MIBCA), Title 53, Marshall Islands Revised Code (MIRC), as amended; ss. 53.05 (Purpose), 53.32 (Articles of Incorporation), 53.34 (name reservation), 53.45 (Registered Office and Registered Agent), 53.63 (Initial Directors), 53.71 (Officers), 53.94 (Action Without Meeting), 53.161 (Certificate of Correction).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Majuro Atoll (filings effected via a licensed Marshall Islands registered agent).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (BC-1) filed with the Registrar of Corporations under MIBCA s. 53.32.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required under the MIBCA. The sole incorporator may subscribe for one or more shares in exchange for such consideration (cash, promissory note, or services) as the Board determines. No escrow account or capital deposit rule applies to non-resident business corporations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation hereby adopts the Articles of Incorporation filed with the Registrar of Corporations and confirms the appointment of the registered agent in the Republic of the Marshall Islands. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Corporation shall be located at the address of the registered agent in Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Corporation authorizes the issuance of One Hundred (100) shares of Common Stock, USD $1.00 par value, to the initial subscriber for aggregate consideration of USD $100.00, fully paid. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following officers are appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Registered Agent Engagement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations (via licensed Marshall Islands registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Reserve the corporate name under MIBCA s. 53.34 by instructing a licensed registered agent in Majuro to submit a name reservation application. The name must end with 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', or an approved abbreviation, and must be distinguishable from all registered names. Execute the agency agreement authorizing the agent to accept service of process and to represent the Corporation before the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Registered agent consent and agency agreement
Corporate KYC and beneficial ownership declaration (agent AML requirement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is rejected for confusing similarity, file a revised reservation adding a distinctive element (e.g., 'MH Global Fleet Technologies Corp.') or obtain written consent from the conflicting entity to allow coexistence on the register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and corporate counsel; ultimate filing with Office of the Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in English stating: (i) the corporate name; (ii) the registered office and registered agent in the RMI; (iii) authorized share capital (e.g., 50,000 common shares at USD $0.001 par value); (iv) an express purpose of any lawful business permitted under MIBCA s. 53.05; and (v) the number and names of the initial directors, if included. Concurrently draft the Bylaws and pre-incorporation share subscription contract for adoption immediately upon incorporation.
required_dossiers: Statement showing names and addresses of initial directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any Registrar query within thirty (30) days by filing amended pages or a Certificate of Correction under MIBCA s. 53.161 to cure scrivener errors without forfeiting the original filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Official Filing and Statutory Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Articles of Incorporation, together with the USD $230.00 state filing fee, either electronically through the registered agent's portal or in paper form at the Majuro registry window. Payment is made by wire transfer or certified cheque through the registered agent. The transmittal may include an exemption notice confirming non-resident status and the absence of any license fee obligation for a foreign-source SaaS corporation.
required_dossiers: Registered agent's signed acceptance of appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns the filing for deficiency, cure any noted defects (e.g., missing signature, incorrect par value statement, incomplete agent consent) and refile within fifteen (15) business days; a late refiling may incur a USD $100.00 administrative surcharge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Organizational Actions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations; office of the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon payment clearance and substantive review, obtain the Certificate of Incorporation from the Registrar. The incorporator then adopts the Bylaws, appoints the initial directors, and each initial director executes a written consent to act. The registered agent retains a certified copy of the Certificate and the organizational consents in the corporate minute book maintained in Majuro.
required_dossiers: Initial directors' written consents to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where an organizational action is defective, ratify it by a subsequent unanimous written consent of incorporator and directors citing MIBCA s. 53.94 (action without meeting), and file a Certificate of Correction if the defect appears on the public record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution, Share Subscription, and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered agent's corporate services office and the Corporate Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or execute the unanimous written consent adopting the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution. The Resolution confirms the subscription for common stock, the registered office address in Majuro, and the appointment of the Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary. Issue the numbered share certificate(s), execute the share subscription contract, receive the USD $100.00 subscription proceeds, and open the corporate records ledger at the registered agent's office.
required_dossiers: Pro-Forma First Board Resolution (or unanimous written consent)
Share subscription agreement and payment confirmation
Registered office confirmation from the agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If share issuance or officer appointments are procedurally defective, pass a corrective board resolution and restate the corporate records; retroactive effectiveness is permitted under MIBCA s. 53.63(4) provided no third-party rights are prejudiced.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable. The Marshall Islands Foreign Investment Board (administered through RMI Trade & Investment) requires no Foreign Investment Business License (FIBL) for a non-resident Business Corporation conducting no commercial activity within the Republic of the Marshall Islands.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — Non-Resident Business Corporation outside FIBL scope; no Marshall Islands operating, manufacturing, or sectoral permit is required for pure cloud-based logistics telematics and fleet dispatch SaaS.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA), Republic of the Marshall Islands
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no EIA registration or Full EIA Report required under the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations. The corporation performs no physical development, land disturbance, or maritime works within RMI territory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to code-only SaaS services, as no wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or solid waste streams are generated. Should the company later deploy physical telematics gateway hardware, dispatch depots, or vehicle fleets within RMI, EPA permitting under the 1991 RMI Environmental Protection Act would apply, including MARPOL-compliant used-oil and battery handling standards and generator emission limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for the non-resident corporation with no physical premises. If an RMI office or data center were established, the RMI Occupational Safety and Health Administration workplace clearance and the Majuro municipal fire safety inspection under the Marshall Islands Fire Safety Act would be required for the workspace, electrical installations, and any rolling stock storage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Marshall Islands Ministry of Finance – Tax and Revenue Office; national portal is not applicable for income-tax registration as the RMI levies no national income tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: No statutory TIN or VAT ID is issued to foreign entities for income-tax or indirect-tax purposes, because the Marshall Islands imposes no corporate income tax and no VAT/GST. Foreign non-resident entities are not required to register for tax on formation or ongoing operations. Employers with local staff must register separately with the Marshall Islands Social Security Administration and obtain a Social Security Registration Number. A Business License is obtained from the Registrar of Corporations solely for regulatory licensing, not taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections exist. The Business Corporation (Non-Resident) is statutorily classified as a non-resident tax-exempt entity; no entity-level or pass-through tax classification is available because the RMI lacks a general income tax statute.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None – no VAT, GST, or sales and use tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable; no indirect tax is imposed and no registration threshold exists.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API filing, or digital stamping regime is imposed by the RMI for domestic or cross-border supplies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable. The Marshall Islands imposes no VAT/GST on domestic or export transactions; therefore there is no 0% export VAT rate and no export zero-rating regime to claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable – no export VAT documentation bundle is required in the absence of an indirect tax system. General customs export declarations may still apply under RMI Customs regulations for goods, but carry no VAT consequence.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Not applicable; no export VAT credit or refund exists, so no export-tax clawback or fraud penalty can arise. General anti-fraud and false-declaration penalties under RMI criminal law may apply to any fraudulent submissions made to the Tax and Revenue Office, but no indirect-tax-specific penalty regime exists.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) Ministry of Finance – Banking Commissioner, appointed under the RMI Banking Act 1991 (as amended), is the de facto financial regulator for banking and foreign exchange prudential matters. No statutory central bank exists; the U.S. Federal Reserve acts as the monetary authority through full dollarization, with the U.S. dollar being the sole legal tender.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The U.S. dollar (USD) is the exclusive legal tender in RMI, making currency convertibility fully obtainable for both current and capital account transactions. There are no statutory exchange-control restrictions on inbound investments or outbound dividend/licensing/profit remittances. Non-resident business corporation accounts may freely move funds in USD or to other currencies without central bank approval. Practical constraints arise solely from bank-level anti-money-laundering (AML) due diligence, the RMI Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism Act 2018, and OFAC sanction screening of all wire traffic.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. RMI law imposes no surrender obligation, statutory timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Receipts may be held indefinitely in USD, converted to third currencies via the correspondent banking network, or settled under bilateral contracts. For AML reporting, local banks must record any cash or wire transaction exceeding USD 10,000, but no forex conversion is mandated.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (USD) and Operational Transaction Account (USD)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Guam – Marshall Islands Branch
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account, Trade Settlement Account, and Commercial Letters of Credit Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low-Medium. The RMI, under the Banking Act 1991, does not have a separate licensing class for electronic money institutions (EMIs) or digital banking providers. Offshore EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Stripe Treasury) cannot act as a direct clearing path into RMI local payment systems and are not treated as banks by the Banking Commissioner. Their permissible use is limited to originating transfers into a licensed BMI or Bank of Guam account, and for settling customer subscription receipts from Stripe Billing/Wire transfers; all final settlement must pass through bank accounts held at a licensed RMI commercial bank or a fully licensed U.S. correspondent.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for all non-resident business corporation account openings. At least one director (or an appointed manager with board resolution) must appear in person at the bank's Majuro or Ebeye branch for the KYC interview. Remote online account opening is not permitted for a BC entity. In exceptional scenarios, a UBO with an existing seven-year or longer banking relationship at BMI may be granted a waiver of the physical interview, subject to enhanced due diligence, notarized corporate ownership charts, and approval by the bank's designated Money Laundering Compliance Officer (MLCO); the waiver process historically requires 10–15 additional business days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) domicile in a jurisdiction identified on the FATF grey/black list or a jurisdiction not compliant with RMI tax information-exchange standards.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive corporate ownership chart from natural persons through the MH_BC structure; certified passport copies; proof of tax residence (tax ID certificate); detailed source-of-wealth affidavit; notarized letter from the enabling agent confirming that non-resident ownership is permissible under RMI Business Corporations Act; three months of professional bank references from the home jurisdiction; shareholder list amendment filings from the RMI Registry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pure offshore SaaS/logistics technology company with no physical business presence in RMI and no requirement for statutory licensing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan with 24-month customer acquisition and cash-flow projections; executed software subscription contracts and Inbound/Outbound telematics service agreements; inventory of IP assets (software registrations, server hosting, trademarks); ISIC 6201 business scope filing; AML risk self-assessment matrix demonstrating low-risk operational pattern; independent verification of beneficial ownership; proof that all corporate secretarial and registered agent documents are current.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection or SaaS settlement wires from digital payment processors (e.g., Stripe Billing) or online EMI platforms, generating a high volume of micro-transactions or refunds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Historical settlement statements from the payment processor covering 90 days; customer dispute/chargeback log and refund policies; reconciliation report between processor payouts and MH_BC operating account; an OFAC standalone clearance report for the payment processor; domain registration and web-server records proving genuine global customer base; a signed statutory director's resolution ratifying payment rail usage and treasury limits.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital subscription funds are injected using the SWIFT MT103 status message from the investor's non-RMI bank to the MH_BC account at a licensed RMI bank. Field 50K contains the full ordering customer name and address; field 56A must be completed with the correspondent BIC when the direct RMI routing path is unavailable. Field 72 must include the secured purpose code 'C' (Capital Contribution) and the unique corporate registration number (e.g., MH_BC registration number). The destination bank will verify the declared purpose against the filed Articles of Association, the RMI Business Corporations Act registration certificate, and a corporate-secretary confirmation letter. If the account is designated as a Capital Escrow Account, disbursement is permitted only after the corporate registry certificate is issued and a director's resolution authorizing the operating account is submitted. No RMI government approval or exchange-control approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement for software licensing royalties, fleet telematics subscriptions, and vendor payments is executed through two primary rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct and recurring disbursements, usually in USD, with a value date at t+0/t+1 and field 70 containing the contract/reference number; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP600 issued through Bank of Guam's trade desk for high-value or documentary settlements, particularly when logistics-fleet equipment or software sublicenses require presentation of invoices, insurance certificates, and proof of delivery (POD). For non-USD counterparts (EUR, JPY, AUD), the treasury manual mandates USD as the functional currency and requires a firm-priced currency conversion quote from the RMI bank before booking; all outbound wires must be OFAC-screened and flagged for the MLCO when the cumulative transaction amount exceeds USD 100,000 in a single business day.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (FX swaps) on USD/EUR, USD/JPY, and USD/AUD, with an underlying commercial invoice or software-lice agreement, subject to standard bank credit documentation and maturity up to 12 months.

Non-deliverable forward contracts (NDFs) for restricted or non-deliverable balance-of-payments currencies (e.g., CNY, INR) used to hedge projected royalty and logistics-tariff exposure when counterparty settlement restrictions exist.

Currency swaps (USD vs foreign currency principal exchange) for multi-year fleet-route licensing contracts, with negative consent from the Banking Commissioner when the notional stranded exposure exceeds USD 15 million.

FX options (purchased, not written) to protect against adverse moves on high-value inbound capital or imminent outbound trade disbursements, with premium paid from the operating account and no speculative resale permitted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Report and Information Statement (Register of Members, Directors, and Officers update)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Marshall Islands Business Entities Registry, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based; due before the anniversary date of incorporation as stated in the Certificate of Incorporation, with a 30-day administrative grace period in normal practice.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of USD 100 per month or fraction thereof, up to a cap of 100% of the annual fee; continued default beyond 90 days after notice permits the Registrar to administratively dissolve or strike off the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise / Exempt Company Consolidated Confirmation (non-resident zero-tax declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Marshall Islands Ministry of Finance and Registrar of Corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based, coinciding with the annual corporate report due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Accruing interest at 1% per month on any unpaid franchise tax balance; failure to file may be certified to the Registrar and lead to loss of good standing, penalty invoicing, and administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandatory for a non-resident Marshall Islands Business Corporation absent an express requirement in the articles, a shareholder resolution, or a lender/investor covenant. A board-approved or contractually required audit may nevertheless be performed for financing, tax review, or group consolidation purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or U.S. GAAP, as adopted by the board; Marshall Islands law permits either framework for statutory record-keeping when no domestic GAAP mandate applies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must obtain and retain current beneficial ownership identification for each shareholder and director; every share transfer or change in control is recorded in the Register of Members and confirmed in the next annual confirmation certificate. A non-resident Business Corporation is not required to lodge the UBO register with the Registrar, but the register must be made available to lawful order of Marshall Islands authorities.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – USD 15,000 when performed for financing or compliance purposes

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for a non-resident domestic exempt corporation licensed under Part II of the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act; 3% ordinary corporate rate applies only to a resident corporation that carries on a trade or business within the Republic of the Marshall Islands.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory income tax exemption for a non-resident domestic corporation: no corporation tax, no advance tax, no withholding tax on dividends, no capital gains tax, and no payroll tax on non-resident sourced earnings. The sole annual fiscal burden is the government license fee of US$250 for authorized capital up to US$50,000, with graduated tiers up to a maximum of US$25,000 for authorized capital exceeding US$200,000,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Renewal Statement & License Fee Form (Registrar of Corporations Form AR-01), filed exclusively through the Marshall Islands Corporate Registry e-portal administered by the Waan Aelõñ Kein Registry Services Division of the Republic of the Marshall Islands.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Annual Renewal Statement and license fee are due on or before the anniversary date of incorporation, no later than the last day of the anniversary month. Each year the filing window opens 60 days before such anniversary and closes on the anniversary; a grace period of 120 days applies before late-surcharge assessment commences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact legal name of the non-resident domestic corporation and its unique eight-character corporate registration number issued by the Registrar of Corporations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the name exactly as stated in the Articles of Incorporation; any corporate name change must be evidenced by the filed Restated Articles or Certificate of Amendment prior to submission.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name of the Marshall Islands-licensed registered agent and the agent's complete physical address in the Republic of the Marshall Islands (not a post-office-box-only address).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The registered agent must remain in good standing; the agent's signature constitutes a valid legal nexus for service of process in the Marshall Islands.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total authorized capital stock in US dollars, parsed by class of shares and par value, and the number of shares of each class issued in the reporting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the stated amount matches the BCA fee schedule; under-declaration of authorized capital to reduce the license fee is a fraudulent misstatement triggering retroactive assessment plus a 10% surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: A statutory declaration confirming that the corporation has not engaged in any trade or business within the Republic of the Marshall Islands and has no source income derived from RMI territory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fleet telematics SaaS revenue derived exclusively from foreign logistics clients is to be declared as non-RMI-source income; use the standard attestation clause affirming absence of RMI shipping, chartering, or local branch activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, postal addresses, and passport or national ID numbers of each current director and of the president, secretary, and treasurer.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directors and officers may be non-residents; no nationality or residency prerequisite exists, but each person must sign a consent-to-act and such consent must be retained by the registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: A declaration of ultimate beneficial owners holding 10% or more of the issued shares or exercising ultimate control by any means, including the nature of such control and the beneficial ownership threshold percentage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident capital structure, identify each natural-person beneficial owner and the top-level parent entity where applicable; nominee shareholder arrangements must be fully transparent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Self-assessment of the annual government license fee based on the authorized capital band, together with the wire-transfer payment receipt or debit authorization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay in US dollars via wire transfer to the account designated by the Registrar of Corporations; the payment is a compliance condition precedent to the issuance of the Certificate of Good Standing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% surcharge on the license fee for the first 120 days of delinquency and an additional 2% per month thereafter. Failure to renew for twenty-four consecutive months results in automatic administrative dissolution by the Registrar, dissolution of the corporate shield, and prohibition from transacting legal business until reinstatement with payment of all arrearages, surcharges, and a reinstatement fee of US$1,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on dividends declared and paid by a non-resident domestic corporation out of non-RMI-source earnings. Dividends paid by a resident RMI corporation to a non-resident shareholder are subject to a 10% gross-basis withholding tax; however, an exempt non-resident domestic corporation is wholly outside the charge to distributed profit tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Marshall Islands has no comprehensive double taxation agreement in force with more than one significant trading partner; its primary bilateral instruments are the Compacts of Free Association with the United States, which do not provide umbrella withholding-tax relief. Where a reduced rate is claimed under any limited bilateral arrangement, the non-resident claimant must submit RMI Form WHT-R to the Chief of Tax and Revenue: attach an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and a statement of beneficial ownership, obtain a prior written determination letter from the Commissioner of Internal Revenue, and present the determination to the withholding agent before the payment date; absent a prior determination, the full statutory rate must be withheld and the excess claimed through refund proceedings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: RMI statutory law imposes a 10% withholding tax on gross interest, rent, and royalty income sourced within the Republic; a 5% reduced rate is available for interest on financial institution loans and arm's-length lease payments under limited bilateral instruments. Because the non-resident domestic corporation's operating income is sourced exclusively outside RMI, outbound payments of royalties and software-subscription license fees and interest paid to foreign lenders will not be subject to RMI-source withholding; the 0% exemption applies to the logistics-telematics SaaS licensing royalty flows.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 0 - the Marshall Islands has no statutory transfer-pricing legislation and imposes no Local File or Master File filing threshold on non-resident domestic corporations. As a defensive practice for an ISIC 6201 software entity, preparation of OECD-aligned benchmarking documentation is recommended where cross-border controlled transactions in the aggregate exceed USD 500,000 annually.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The RMI Economic Substance Regulations apply effective January 1, 2022. A non-resident domestic corporation that does not claim tax residency in a foreign jurisdiction must demonstrate: (i) registered office and core management physically present in the Marshall Islands, (ii) adequate qualified employees proportionate to its fleet-dispatch telematics business, (iii) sufficient non-resident operating expenditure in RMI, and (iv) no outsourcing of core income-generating activities. A company that is subject to corporate income tax in the United States, Hong Kong SAR, or another approved jurisdiction and files an annual foreign-residency declaration is exempted from the RMI substantive test. Failure to prove economic substance where claimed exposes 100% of the exempt company's foreign-derived income to recharacterization as taxable RMI-source profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Exemption Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing RMI-source activity, falsely declaring non-resident status while a server, sales office, or maritime dispatch management is physically located within the Republic, or knowingly underdeclaring authorized capital to reduce the annual license fee.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Title 19 of the RMI Income Tax Act, conviction carries a fine of up to US$25,000 for the corporation, treble the amount of the tax underpaid, and a 50% accuracy-related penalty upon the underpayment; the registrar may also impose a 10% surcharge on assessed deficiencies for false statements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or authorize the false annual renewal statement are jointly and severally liable for the corporation's unpaid taxes and penalties; the RMI Attorney-General may pursue a personal restitution order, impose a travel ban, and a custodial penalty of up to five years for each officer who wilfully participated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the RMI entity as a tokenized nameplate in global fleet-dispatch SaaS procurement, with no premises, no staffing, no RMI bank account, and management fully conducted abroad, while using the RMI tax-exempt status as the sole commercial advantage.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The RMI Government, through the Registrar of Corporations, may administratively dissolve the entity for lack of economic substance, strike its name from the Corporate Registry, and deny the Certificate of Good Standing used in banking and government procurement; foreign tax authorities may disregard the RMI entity and impose full CFC or controlled-foreign-corporation inclusion of profits with a 20% negligence penalty each year of default.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts in the Marshall Islands and foreign fora may pierce the corporate veil where the entity is a facade: directors become personally liable for the entire stream of foreign taxes otherwise due from the company; travel restrictions may be issued to preserve jurisdiction; directors are exposed to de facto joint debt liability for all SaaS subscription contracts entered in the entity's name.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file a true and complete beneficial ownership statement within 30 days of any change in ownership or control; use of bearer shares; concealment of the ultimate controller through a chain of opaque nominee entities; omission of the 10% threshold declaration in the annual renewal statement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Business Corporations Act (as amended by the Beneficial Ownership Regulations), the Registrar may levy a civil fine of US$10,000 plus a US$2,000 monthly penalty for continuing default; the company is subject to automatic suspension from the Corporate Registry and its registered agent may be compelled to resign, triggering non-solvency under service contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Each director and officer who knowingly permits the filing of a false beneficial ownership statement is personally liable for the maximum statutory fine and may be disqualified from serving as a director of any RMI company for a period of ten years; a criminal conviction for false declaration exposes the director to twelve months' imprisonment alongside the civil monetary penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain any arm's-length intercompany agreement for the provision of software licensing and logistics IP between the RMI non-resident entity and a foreign affiliate or parent; the RMI company bears no personnel and never performs a demonstrable business function, while high-tax authorities allocate all risk and profit by substance-over-form. The absence of transfer-pricing files in the OECD format deepens the exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A foreign competent authority will apply a transfer-pricing adjustment that treats the RMI entity as a shell branch of the parent, disallowing deductions for royalty/license fees paid to the RMI entity and assessing the profits in the corporate taxpayer's home jurisdiction; a transactional penalty of 35% of the adjusted amount is common under major tax systems; the RMI government will not deliver treaty protection absent a comprehensive DTA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the foreign parent who sign the consolidated tax return and documentation declaring the RMI entity as a distinctive business, knowingly without economic substance, face personal liability for the foreign revenue authority's assessment in the form of a director penalty; the tax authority can enforce against personal bank accounts, order deportation or travel bans into the source country where the director resides, and initiate criminal proceedings for tax fraud with imprisonment up to seven years in the taxpayer's jurisdiction.
